indicators.note: in a down clue, upset says the pieces are turned upside down, so read from the bottom up

parts.note: MR is the abbreviation for motivational research
provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'

explanation.surface: A company's market research was upset by some proviso.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a company or commercial enterprise, a synonym for a business.

parts.note: a lover is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: A student's partner owns a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing leguminous plant with three-part leaves, an example of the category.

clue.text: Faint-hearted individuals taking a time away from capital

indicators.note: taking ... away from tells us to remove the stated letters from the capital
with taking, away from names the city as the word losing letters

parts.note: Athens is the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: Timid people are leaving the capital for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... away from' removes A and T from ATHENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickens, and by extension hens, stand for cowards; a chicken is a timid, faint-hearted person.

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a.p., ante prandium, is the old prescription abbreviation for 'before a meal'

explanation.surface: A photo of a lunch tin taken before eating.
explanation.walkthrough: AP is Latin ante prandium, once written on prescriptions for a dose taken before meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal photograph, a snapshot, so a picture.

clue.text: Boney M disembarked from converted monoplane

indicators.note: the letter M is said to get off the aircraft, so it is taken out of the fodder
converted says the remaining letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

parts.note: the M of the pop group's name is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A member of the disco group Boney M climbs out of a refitted single-winged aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: MONOPLANE without M leaves ONOPLANE, which 'converted' rearranges. Boney M were a 1970s disco group.
explanation.definitionFit: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon Bonaparte, the French emperor.

parts.note: Uriel is one of the archangels

explanation.surface: A young woman has wed an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: Muriel is also the goat in Orwell's Animal Farm, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Muriel is a female given name, so an example of a girl's name.

parts.note: US stands for the United States, hence American
a century is a long period, and an age is too; the question mark marks the loose example

explanation.surface: How the hundred years of American dominance were handled.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls 'the American Century', the twentieth century as one of US dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is handled or used, so it is a synonym of treatment.

clue.text: Permission to cross the Incredible Hulk, say?

definitions.meaning: the lit figure at a pedestrian crossing that tells walkers they may go
the comic-book giant has green skin, so he is literally a man coloured green

explanation.surface: Is a superhero's go-ahead needed to cross the road?
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the walking-figure crossing signal and, playfully, any figure whose skin is that colour, like the Marvel character.

clue.text: Writer's stomach, after accepting European source of gold?

indicators.note: accepting says the first word takes in the next piece

parts.note: gorge is an old word for the stomach or gullet
or is the heraldic word for gold
a well is a source, as of water or oil

explanation.surface: A writer's appetite after taking a European gold mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of gold' gives the pieces in reverse order: WELL of OR, i.e. OR then WELL. Orwell wrote Animal Farm, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Blair wrote under this pen name, so the answer is an example of a writer.

parts.note: an arm is a limb, one of the body's members

explanation.surface: A woman is told to grow something on her limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To farm land is to cultivate it, growing crops; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Vehicle Inspectorate returned left over square instruments

parts.note: VI is the abbreviation for the Vehicle Inspectorate, the former UK testing agency

indicators.note: returned says the pair of letters beside it is turned back to front

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
S is taken as an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Vehicle inspectors sent back leftover square instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LO into OL. The Vehicle Inspectorate tested lorries and cars in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Viols are bowed stringed instruments of the Renaissance, precursors of the violin family.

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is the usual crossword source for books

explanation.surface: A public library has a plan for its books.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan or conspiracy, a synonym of scheme.

indicators.note: describing is used in its sense of drawing round, so the remark encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: a jeer is a mocking remark

explanation.surface: A clown's mocking comment about a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its sense of drawing a line round something.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was a court fool, a professional clown, so a buffoon.

parts.note: fruit that is ripe has reached its fully developed best state

explanation.surface: A rubbish singer has supposedly reached perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, literally offal, is slang for worthless talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Increasingly despondent note left Romeo agitated, I admitted

parts.note: G is one of the musical notes

indicators.note: admitted says the shuffled letters take in the single letter
agitated says the letters of the word Romeo are stirred up

explanation.surface: A message left Romeo upset, and he became gloomier as he confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns ROMEO into OOMER; 'admitted' puts I inside it to make OOMIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative form means more downcast than before, so it matches increasingly despondent.

clue.text: Have to thank old people in general

parts.note: we can stand for people at large, as in 'we all make mistakes'

explanation.surface: We should be grateful to the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe someone thanks is to be indebted, which is having to thank them.

clue.text: Medical officer initially sedated El Salvador man with tablets

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A doctor sedated a Salvadoran patient on pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tablets' looks medical; it is the stone tablets of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses brought down the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments from Sinai.

indicators.note: backfired suggests going into reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or plate

explanation.surface: A beast's thin armour plating failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute can mean any beast, as opposed to a human, a synonym of animal.

clue.text: Inform aircraftsman in the capacity of popular troop leader

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for aircraftsman in the RAF
qua is Latin for 'as', in the capacity of
in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of troop

explanation.surface: Telling an airman that he is a well-liked platoon commander.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with something is to make them familiar with it, i.e. tell them.

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone at the tryout was dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person but is the verb to drill.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool that pierces holes in leather or wood; bore is used as a noun-like tool sense.

clue.text: Self-conscious being by himself working for euros, primarily

indicators.note: for says one thing takes the place of another

parts.note: per se is Latin for by itself, in itself

indicators.note: primarily takes the opening letter of euros

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A self-aware man working alone in exchange for euros.
explanation.walkthrough: PER SE has its E (euros, primarily) swapped for ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is a human individual, a being aware of itself.

clue.text: One who sings about equalisers is ejected

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around
is ejected tells us the little word is thrown out of the fodder before rearranging

parts.note: taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A singer, apparently on the subject of goals that level the score, gets sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: EQUALISERS without IS leaves EQUALERS, rearranged. Squealer is the propagandist pig in Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A squealer is an informer, someone who sings to the police, slang for telling.

clue.text: Ignore idiot in empty pub yard

indicators.note: in puts the fool inside the emptied pub
empty leaves only the outside letters of pub

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Ignore the fool in the deserted pub garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass someone by is to take no notice of them, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Private detectives beginning to tease small birds

parts.note: a PI is a private investigator, and two of them give the plural
the second private investigator

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of tease

explanation.surface: Detectives start to tease little birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small birds' looks like the whole definition, but small gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipits are small brown songbirds such as the meadow pipit.

indicators.note: following says the hesitation comes after the other piece

parts.note: being in a box means being in a tight spot
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A boxer hesitates when in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxer is the loyal carthorse in Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a prize fighter in the ring.

indicators.note: recalled in the sense of called back, sending the word backwards

parts.note: to run drugs is to traffic them, so ran
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A US drugs officer remembered smuggled coke.
explanation.walkthrough: The DEA is the US Drug Enforcement Administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Narc is American slang for a narcotics officer, such as one in the DEA.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades, the card suit

explanation.surface: A firm uses shovels to threaten people.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Easily-led sorts look around hospital parking

indicators.note: around says the first word goes round the next

parts.note: to see is to look
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Gullible people look around the hospital car park.
explanation.definitionFit: People who follow the crowd without thought are called sheep, an idiomatic figurative sense.

indicators.note: leaving says those letters depart from the healer's name

parts.note: a shaman is a tribal healer or medicine man
AN is taken as a short form of Angola

explanation.surface: A bogus healer departs from Angola.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fraud or counterfeit, a synonym of fake.

indicators.note: found in says the animal sits inside the code

parts.note: PY is the international code for Paraguay
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A beast with spots is discovered in Paraguay.
explanation.definitionFit: Poxy literally means covered in pock-marks, i.e. pimply.

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of priggish

explanation.surface: Strangely prim greedy eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling greedy eaters by the farmyard animal name is an idiomatic metaphor for overeaters.

definitions.meaning: a ball of packed snow, a missile in a playful 'cold war' fight
to grow ever faster, as a rolling ball of snow gathers more

explanation.surface: A weapon of the Cold War stockpile is being built up.
explanation.walkthrough: Snowball is also the exiled pig in Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed ball of snow is thrown in winter fights, and to snowball is to grow rapidly.

clue.text: Flashy vulgarians' row enthrals German society

indicators.note: enthrals is read as holding captive, so the row holds the next piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A showy crowd's quarrel captivates a German club.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives tiger as slang for a flashy, vulgarly showy person.
